cards.front: Recall a key point about Photographers and Photography History
cards.back: Photography's history: from daguerreotypes to digital, each technical advance changed what and how photographers could communicate.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Photographers and Photography History
cards.back: Key movements: pictorialism (soft, painterly), straight photography (sharp, unmanipulated), modernism (formal experimentation), postmodernism (conceptual, appropriated).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Photographers and Photography History
cards.back: Photography has enormous social and cultural impact — it shapes how we see the world, from photojournalism to advertising to social media.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Photographers and Photography History
cards.back: Understanding why and how photographers work helps you make more informed, intentional choices in your own practice.

cards.front: What should you know about photography exam tips?
cards.back: Always include: photographer NAME, photograph TITLE, DATE. Analyse using VISUAL LANGUAGE (composition, lighting, viewpoint). Explain CONTEXT — when/where/why. Show your PERSONAL RESPONSE — how has this research changed your own approach?

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Photography history is irrelevant — I just need to take good pictures. Correct: Understanding photography's history gives you a VISUAL VOCABULARY and CONTEXT for your own choices.
